clue.text: Not the main route in foreign parts

definitions.meaning: ... in Britain is a secondary road, not one of the main A-roads, so the phrase reads as ...

explanation.surface: Someone abroad prefers to wander off the beaten track rather than take the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are classed A (main) and B (secondary), so 'not the main route' is a B-road, and 'a B-road' run together is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in foreign parts means being overseas, away from one's home country.

clue.text: Does it take root in pipeclay?

definitions.text: Does it take root in pipeclay?

parts.words: Does it take root in pipeclay?
parts.note: tobacco pipes are made either of clay or of the woody root of a heath shrub; the clue asks whether that root wood takes the place of pipeclay

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a plant can grow roots in a bed of white clay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a plant rooting in clay soil; in fact pipes are carved from the root of the heath plant, a rival material to the clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Briar is the root wood of the tree heath, used for tobacco pipes in place of clay.

clue.text: Not many top jobs in this government

definitions.text: Not many top jobs in this government

parts.words: Not many top jobs in this government
parts.note: a state where power sits with a small few, so only a handful hold the top posts

explanation.surface: A complaint that the administration offers few senior posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by a small group of people means only a few hold power.

clue.text: One way to get around

parts.note: a roundabout route that takes you around an obstacle such as roadworks

explanation.surface: Advice on a method of travelling about.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a route that takes you around a blocked road.

clue.text: Print from the film to be sure

definitions.meaning: a photographic print made from the negative

explanation.surface: A photographer checks the print against the film to be quite certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic print is made from a negative, and being certain is being sure.

clue.text: What crack-pot inventors discover in Tennyson's brook

definitions.text: What crack-pot inventors discover in Tennyson's brook

parts.words: What crack-pot inventors discover in Tennyson's brook
parts.note: Tennyson's poem The Brook has the refrain 'I go on for ever'; cranks keep trying to build a machine that runs for ever

explanation.surface: Eccentric inventors finding something in the stream of Tennyson's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's The Brook repeats 'For men may come and men may go, But I go on for ever', which is the endless running that crank inventors seek in vain.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that runs for ever without energy input is the impossible dream of crank inventors.

clue.text: Cause of a hold-up in window-dressing

definitions.text: Cause of a hold-up in window-dressing

parts.words: Cause of a hold-up in window-dressing
parts.note: a hold-up here is the holding up of a sliding window, done by the line running over its pulley; window-dressing is the frame fittings, not a shop display

explanation.surface: Why the shop window display has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a delay and 'window-dressing' a shop display; really the line in a sash window's frame holds the pane up.
explanation.definitionFit: The line attached to a sliding window's weights keeps the pane raised.

clue.text: To them dropping an aitch is something symbolic

indicators.note: dropping says a letter falls out of the words before it, as in a careless accent

parts.note: aitch is the name of the letter H

explanation.surface: To some speakers, dropping their H's carries social meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes H out of TO THEM, as a Cockney drops aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem, an object standing for a clan or idea.

clue.text: Even trade can be held in respect

indicators.note: can be suggests these letters could be turned into something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fair dealing earns a business a good reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges the letters of EVEN TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venerated means revered, regarded with great esteem.

clue.text: Not great works of art, evidently

definitions.text: Not great works of art, evidently

parts.words: Not great works of art, evidently
parts.note: not great is read literally as small in size, so tiny paintings rather than poor ones

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing some paintings as mediocre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not great' sounds like a judgment of quality; it means small in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny paintings, often portraits, are small-scale works of art.

clue.text: Holders of wine, or nuts perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word nuts may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Barrels of wine, or bowls of nuts, on a sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Large casks used for holding wine or beer.

clue.text: Steel plates, for instance, "are almost fully developed

indicators.note: almost means the word are is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: fully developed means grown up or ripe

explanation.surface: Steel plates are nearly ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel plates' looks like the subject of a sentence; it is the definition, armour plating being one kind of protective covering. The stray opening quote mark is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: An armature is protective covering, such as metal plating on a ship or animal.

clue.text: Picture-maker, one from America possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of America, less the one taken from them, are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: A photographer whose equipment may have come from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one from' takes I out of AMERICA, leaving AMERCA, and 'possibly' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that takes photographs makes pictures.

clue.text: Not happy with this music on so late

definitions.text: Not happy with this music on so late

parts.words: Not happy with this music on so late
parts.note: a neighbour annoyed at a record being played late at night; split another way, the opening words also hint at the ... of someone hearing a record put on

explanation.surface: A neighbour complains about music being played late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is the thing playing the music.

clue.text: Refuge for misogynists ?

parts.note: woman-haters would want an island inhabited only by males, read from the name of an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Somewhere for those who dislike women to escape to.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is a real self-governing island between Britain and Ireland; its name is read literally as an island of males.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's name, taken literally, describes a place for men only.

clue.text: Posts for honest men ?

definitions.meaning: vertical poles, such as goalposts or door jambs

explanation.surface: Jobs suitable for people of integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' looks like jobs; it means vertical poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertical supports are uprights, and straight-dealing people are called upright.

clue.text: After turn, of month hastened to right man to secure overdraft

indicators.note: turn says the short form of the month is turned backwards

parts.note: AUG is the abbreviation for August
hastened means ran

explanation.surface: At the start of a new month, someone rushes to find a backer for a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses AUG to GUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pledges to pay if a borrower defaults secures the bank's loan.

clue.text: Country with smallest population

parts.note: smallest refers to the size of the people, not their number: the land of tiny people in Swift's Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A trivia question about the least populous nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smallest population' suggests fewest inhabitants; it means the tiniest people.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the island's inhabitants are six inches tall.

clue.text: Does the theatrical producer foot it?

definitions.text: Does the theatrical producer foot it?

parts.words: Does the theatrical producer foot it?
parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it, and a show's printed poster is a bill the producer pays for

explanation.surface: Asking whether the impresario pays the costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot it' recalls footing the bill, here a theatre's printed bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A poster or programme advertising a play is a printed notice of the show.

clue.text: Lover's handyman

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the author's name is followed by a word that has the answer held inside it

explanation.surface: A partner's useful odd-job man.
explanation.walkthrough: Lover is the Irish novelist Samuel Lover, not a sweetheart; his comic novel Handy Andy has this bungling servant as its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Lover's best-known character, the title hero of Handy Andy, so the author's name stands for his creation.

clue.text: One way round the problem of the broken belt

definitions.text: One way round the problem of the broken belt

parts.words: One way round the problem of the broken belt
parts.note: if your belt snaps, you could tie a length of cord round your waist instead

explanation.surface: A fix for a snapped belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cord tied around the waist can stand in for a belt.

clue.text: A little food with some rum .or seltzer

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snack served with a drink of rum or soda water.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bite or mouthful.

clue.text: Swell point to press

parts.note: S is the compass point south
to press means to urge

explanation.surface: A fine point to press home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an adjective meaning splendid; it is a verb or noun for a rising rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden swelling rush, as of the sea.

clue.text: Lowest grade of actors in open-air theatres ?

definitions.text: Lowest grade of actors in open-air theatres ?

parts.words: Lowest grade of actors in open-air theatres ?
parts.note: actors performing outdoors form a cast that is out, and the lowest grade of society is those outside the caste system

explanation.surface: A question about the humblest performers at outdoor theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: Outdoor performers are an 'out cast'; Indian society's outcasts stood outside and below the castes.
explanation.definitionFit: People rejected by society, outside every caste, are the lowest grade.

clue.text: Rigid verbal form ?

definitions.meaning: a form of a verb showing time, such as past or future

explanation.surface: A complaint about stiff, formal wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal' looks like spoken; it means of verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut muscles are rigid, and past or present is a grammatical form of a verb.

clue.text: A half-glass for the Eastern potentate

indicators.note: half says only the first part of the glass word is kept

parts.note: a glass is a looking-glass, a mirror

explanation.surface: Half a glass of something offered to a sheikh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps MIR from MIRROR; 'glass' means a looking-glass, not a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, and this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Milton's neat-handed girl, flower of the north, sounds a materialist

indicators.note: sounds says the two names, said together, are heard as another word

parts.words: Milton's neat-handed girl, flower of the north
parts.note: in Milton's poem L'Allegro, 'neat-handed Phillis' dresses the dinner; a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tyne flows through north-east England

explanation.surface: A girl from Milton's poem and a northern bloom sound like an uncultured person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river (a thing that flows), here the Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A person indifferent to art and culture, caring only for material things.

clue.text: Like the silent drum — this record still stands.

definitions.meaning: a drum nobody has struck is quiet
a record not yet surpassed by anyone

explanation.surface: An image of a silent drum beside a sporting record that has not been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a disc; it is a best performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum not struck is silent, and a record nobody has surpassed remains undefeated.

clue.text: Scene of the first eviction order

definitions.text: Scene of the first eviction order

parts.words: Scene of the first eviction order
parts.note: in Genesis, Adam and Eve are expelled from Eden, the first people ever thrown out of their home

explanation.surface: Where the earliest notice to quit was served.
explanation.walkthrough: The eviction is the expulsion from Eden in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden was the paradise from which Adam and Eve were driven out.
